affected_flow: client -> AdminService/SQL (any Kerberos SPN account with a weak/static password)
official_mitigation: use gMSA/dMSA for service accounts (gMSA: 240-byte / 120-character random password changed every 30 days) so offline cracking of a requested service ticket is infeasible; require AES service-ticket encryption
detection: Windows Security event 4769: monitor ticket encryption types other than 0x11/0x12 (AES), e.g. 0x17 RC4-HMAC; check for one user requesting many service tickets for Kerberoasting-prone accounts in a short time; Defender for Identity alert external ID 2410 (suspected Kerberos SPN exposure)

affected_flow: site/ci flows that could fall back to NTLM against LDAP/AD CS/SMB if Kerberos is unavailable
official_mitigation: Extended Protection for Authentication (channel binding over TLS, or SPN-based service binding) for HTTPS/LDAPS: on by default in Exchange Server 2019 CU14 and for AD CS and LDAP on Windows Server 2025 (LDAP channel binding 'When Supported'); plan for NTLM being disabled by default in a future Windows version
detection: Windows 11 24H2 / Windows Server 2025 enhanced NTLM auditing in Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational (client 4020/4021; server 4022/4023; DC 4030-4033): Warning level for NTLMv1 use; EPA not supported or insecure; or MIC not used

attack_class: Token theft / replay (stolen refresh or access token used from another device)
affected_flow: client MSAL delegated tokens; site app-only tokens
official_mitigation: Token Protection (only device-bound sign-in session tokens such as the PRT are accepted; native apps on supported platforms); short access-token lifetimes; CAE critical-event revocation
detection: Entra sign-in logs show token issued from an unexpected device/IP; CAE claim-challenge flow (401 + claim) surfaces a rejected-but-not-yet-expired token
sources: S1227 (DOC: Token Protection accepts only device-bound sign-in session tokens); S1347 (DER: CAE's claim-challenge mechanism is the documented detection/response path for a token a resource provider wants to reject)

attack_class: Consent phishing (malicious app tricking a user into granting delegated Graph consent)
affected_flow: client engineer using MSAL delegated Graph calls
official_mitigation: restrict user consent to verified publishers and low-risk permissions; publisher verification; admin consent workflow for consent requests; app governance policies
detection: Entra audit logs for consent grants; Defender for Cloud Apps OAuth app and anomaly policies; apps Microsoft disabled show DisabledDueToViolationOfServicesAgreement

attack_class: SMB coercion (forcing a machine account to authenticate to an attacker-controlled listener)
affected_flow: site instance reading a artifact share over SMB; any host with the print spooler or similar coercion-capable service reachable
official_mitigation: disable the Print Spooler service on domain controllers and AD admin systems (and any server that does not need it); SMB signing; block inbound NTLM where not needed
detection: Defender for Identity alert 'Suspected DFSCoerce attack using Distributed File System Protocol' (external ID 2426); Defender for Identity security assessment for the Print spooler service on domain controllers
